title: The actor model: isolated state and message passing

videos.script: Two desks, one copy of a book, and both of them lend it. {{desks}} Neither desk did anything wrong. The bug lives between a check and an act, when two threads share one shelf. {{gap}} This lesson takes the sharing away. The shelf gets an owner, and the owner is an actor. {{actor}} An actor has a mailbox, private state and one rule. It handles one message at a time, from start to finish. {{mailbox}} You will build one from a thread and a queue, and watch the same race fail to happen. {{build}} Then you will ask an actor a question, and see how an actor can wait for itself for ever. {{ask}} Next comes failure. When an actor crashes, its supervisor starts a fresh one. You will see exactly what the fresh one forgets. {{supervisor}} Finally the shelf moves into another process, and the code that talks to it does not change. {{process}} That is why actors talk in messages and never in calls. The last section shows the same ideas in Akka, in Go and in Erlang.
